title: Correct frictional force (part 1)
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) is 0.72 N, derived from the static friction needed to accelerate the weight with the cardboard.

title: Correct fall-off time (part 2)
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) is 0.4 s, obtained from solving the relative motion equation.

title: Identify friction regimes
description: Important: Recognizes that for F=1.9 N, the weight and cardboard move together without slipping, so friction is static.

title: Apply relative motion equation
description: Important: For part (2), sets up the correct equation relating the relative acceleration and distance: (1/2)a₂t² - (1/2)a₁t² = d.

title: Calculate accelerations correctly
description: Important: Correctly computes a₁ = μg for the slipping weight and a₂ = (F - F_f2 - F_f1')/m₂ for the cardboard in part (2).

title: Determine maximum static friction
description: Optional: Compares the required static friction force (0.72 N) to the maximum possible static friction (μ m₁g = 0.8 N) to verify no slipping in part (1).

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Maintains consistent use of SI units (N, kg, m, s) throughout the solution.

title: Confuse static and kinetic friction
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly uses kinetic friction (0.8 N) for the weight in part (1) when the system accelerates together.

title: Sign error in relative motion
description: Pitfall: Uses an incorrect sign in the relative displacement equation (e.g., a₁t²/2 - a₂t²/2 = d) leading to a wrong time.

title: Forget friction on cardboard
description: Pitfall: Omits the kinetic friction force F_f2 = μ(m₁+m₂)g when calculating the cardboard's acceleration in part (2).
